through changing trade equations, uncertain 
market signals, rising input pressures and 
shifting global economic trends – with clarity 
and consistency.
Through changing tides, 
the course remained clear.

At Avanti, that direction was set by our Founder, 
Sri Alluri Venkateswara Rao through values that continue 
to guide the Company across changing times: integrity, 
responsibility, resilience and inclusive progress.
His vision did not merely build an enterprise. It created a 
way of working – one that places trust before transaction, 
quality before compromise, and long-term value before 
short-term advantage.
As Avanti enters new markets, strengthens new categories 
and navigates new possibilities, this legacy remains our 
compass.
It keeps the Company anchored in purpose, even as it 
charts growth across changing tides.
Legacy as 
	 Our Compass
Every enduring journey begins with direction.
• 

A Test of Adaptability
What emerged through this period of transition 
was not merely a test of scale – it was a test of 
adaptability. The ability to respond to change 
without losing direction.
Even as parts of the environment remained volatile, 
the fundamentals of global seafood demand 
stayed intact. Consumption patterns evolved. 
Supply chains recalibrated. Markets adjusted. 
And within that movement, Avanti stayed 
firmly anchored in what has always defined the 
Company: product quality, farmer engagement, 
and the depth of relationship that does not 
fracture under pressure.
In an industry where confidence at  
the farm level is everything, consistency  
became the Company’s greatest  
competitive advantage.
Charting Growth 
	 Across Changing Tides.
There are years that reward momentum.  
And there are years that test conviction.
FY 2025–26 was the second kind.
Trade equations rewrote themselves during the year. Tariff structures in key export 
markets altered established demand patterns. Geopolitical tensions in West Asia dis-
rupted shipping routes, extended transit timelines, and raised freight and insurance 
costs. Across markets, uncertainty travelled faster than cargo.
The tides were changing. Avanti was charting.
6 | Annual Report 2025-26 

The Feed business grew profitability by 8% on a near-flat revenue base – while 
cutting feed prices to support farmers. The Processing business grew revenues by 
43% through a year when the largest single export market imposed a 50% tariff. 
Earnings Per Share grew 12.75%. The balance sheet: remained strong with negligible 
debt. 
These are not numbers that survive a difficult year. These are numbers that grow 
through one.
The Chart Ahead
The year also marked a decisive shift in the Company’s export geography. 
Avanti expanded its presence across Japan, Korea, the European Union, the Middle 
East and Canada – building the market depth that makes a business genuinely 
resilient, not merely large. When one door narrows, another window is already open.
And beyond the core, Avanti is opening new waters entirely.
The Avant Furst pet care brand – built on thirty years of expertise in nutrition, 
sourcing, processing and quality – is entering a fast-growing consumer category 
with long-term structural appeal. Revenue has scaled fourfold across the first three 
quarters of the year. A manufacturing facility near Hyderabad begins production in 
2028. An European subsidiary is in progress. Every initiative is self-funded.
The global aquaculture industry will keep evolving.
Trade dynamics will shift. Supply chains will adapt. New geographies will open; 
familiar ones will change their terms. The businesses that create enduring value in 
this environment will not be the ones that simply move forward – but the ones that 
know how to navigate change.
That is the knowledge Avanti carries. Thirty years deep.
And it is precisely how the Company continues to chart its  
growth across changing tides.

Resilience, today, is not built through capacity alone. It is built 
through adaptability, market intelligence, and the willingness to 
move before the tide forces you to.

Reading the Currents
FY 2025-26 was not a year of a single challenge.
It was a year of multiple currents moving at once.
A 50% tariff on Indian goods into the United States – the largest single 
shrimp export market – altered the economics of exports mid-year. 
West Asia-related disruptions rewired shipping routes, extended transit 
time lines, and raised freight and insurance costs. In the feed business, 
higher Peruvian fish catches eased fish meal prices significantly, helping 
moderate raw material pressures. The appreciation of the US dollar 
Reading the Currents 
	 The year in Perspective
8 | Annual Report 2025-26 

provided support to export realisations, even as demand signals remained 
uneven across geographies.
At the same time, the global shrimp market began to show signs of better 
pricing discipline and renewed demand across select destinations.
For Avanti, the year demanded more than operational efficiency.
It demanded judgement.
When to hold. When to recalibrate. When to protect farmer economics. 
When to deepen customer relationships. When to build beyond the 
familiar.
The Company responded through disciplined execution, a wider market 
approach, stronger value-added focus, and continued investment in 
future-facing categories.
This was not growth in calm waters.
It was growth shaped by the ability to read the currents – and move with 
purpose.
Three Currents. One Response.
The U.S. Tariff Environment
The reciprocal tariff structure – rising from 26% in April 2025 to 50% by 
August 2025 – materially altered the economics of Indian shrimp exports 
to the U.S. market. Avanti responded through a dual strategy: passing on 
the tariff impact to U.S. buyers where commercially feasible, and simul-
taneously accelerating market diversification across Japan, Korea, the 
European Union, the Middle East and Canada. 
The year closed with a landmark ruling. The U.S. Supreme Court ruled on 
20th February 2026 – by a 6–3 majority – that the International Emergency 
Economic Powers Act does not authorise the imposition of tariffs. This 
invalidated the reciprocal duty structure and initiated a refund process. 
Shipping and Logistics
Geopolitical tensions in West Asia disrupted the Red Sea–Suez Canal 
corridor through much of the year, extending transit times and raising 
freight rates and marine insurance costs. Avanti responded through 
proactive logistics planning, vessel routing flexibility and consolidated 
freight management – absorbing much of the disruption without com-
promising delivery commitments to customers.
Raw Material Costs
Fish meal and soya bean meal – the two most critical inputs to shrimp 
feed – moved steadily higher through FY 2025-26. Through weighted-
average inventory management and disciplined procurement, Avanti 
managed these increases while maintaining feed quality – and the feed 
division delivered its best PBT in recent years.

Widening the Map.  
	 Balancing the Course.
In global seafood, dependence on a single 
market is not merely a strategic risk. It is a 
vulnerability that compounds under pressure. 
FY 2025–26 made this clear. With the United 
States — historically the largest buyer of 
Indian shrimp — facing a sharply altered tariff 
environment, the economics of concentrated 
export dependence came under pressure 
across the industry.
For Avanti Frozen Foods, the year tested 
a strategy already in motion. Over recent 
years, the Company had steadily widened its 
customer base across the European Union, 
Japan, Korea, the Middle East and Canada. 
These relationships were not built after the 
disruption arrived; they were already part of 
a deliberate effort to create market resilience.
The result was a more balanced export 
platform. While U.S. shrimp export volumes 
across the industry declined 17.9%, Avanti’s 
processing revenues grew 43%. At the 
industry level, Europe and Japan also gained 
momentum, reinforcing the importance of 
diversified market access.
This was not diversification in reaction to 
disruption. It was diversification that made 
the Company ready for it. Every new market 
adds more than volume — it adds resilience, 
optionality, and balance. 
India’s Seafood Exports —  
A Record Year
India’s seafood exports touched a record 
`73,890.46 crore, or USD 8.46 billion, in 
FY 2025–26, with shipments of 19.72 lakh 
metric tonnes. Frozen shrimp remained the 
lead category, contributing 40.19% of export 
volume and 66.52% of export earnings. The 
appreciation of the US dollar during the year 
also benefited export-oriented companies 
such as Avanti substantially, supporting 
rupee realisations and helping strengthen 
overall export economics. The Course Ahead
Three structural developments reinforce 
export opportunity through FY 2026–27 and 
beyond. The India–EU Free Trade Agreement, 
when ratified, will progressively reduce 
tariffs of up to 26% on Indian shrimp into the 
world's largest seafood market. The India–
UK CETA provides 100% duty-free access 
to the UK. And the bilateral understanding 
of February 2026 has reduced the effective 
US tariff to 18% — a significant recovery from 
the 50% peak. Avanti has also established 
a UK subsidiary to take advantage of the 
emerging trade opportunities arising from 
these favourable tariff developments.
Avanti Frozen Foods is also pursuing refunds 
of tariffs collected during the invalidated 
reciprocal 
duty 
period, 
estimated 
at 
approximately USD 15–20 million, subject 
to validation, administrative review and 
applicable U.S. Customs processes. 
The map is wider. The course is more 
balanced. Avanti is better positioned to chart 
growth across changing tides.

Anchored in Feed Leadership 
Shrimp Feed Division
At the heart of Avanti's journey is its shrimp 
feed business – the foundation on which 
the Company built its reputation, farmer 
relationships and industry leadership over 
three decades.
In FY 2025-26, the feed business operated 
through a challenging environment. Raw 
material 
prices 
increased 
through 
the 
year, while market conditions limited the 
immediate ability to pass on the full cost 
impact. Considering global uncertainties 
and for sustainability of aquaculture in April 
2025, the Company reduced feed prices 
to support farmer economics – reinforcing 
its 
long-standing 
commitment 
to 
the 
aquaculture community.
Despite 
near-flat 
revenue, 
the 
division 
improved profitability, reflecting operating 
discipline, 
procurement 
efficiency 
and 
sustained trust across the farming ecosystem.
The numbers tell one part of the story. The 
stronger story lies in the relationships behind 
them.
For thousands of farmers, Avanti feed is not 
merely an input. It is confidence in every 
pond. It is consistency through every crop 
cycle. It is reliable technical support when 
conditions change. That trust continues to 
anchor Avanti's leadership.
A Headwind That Will Be Navigated
The closing months of FY 2025-26 and 
the opening of FY 2026-27 brought a 
significant cost shock. Fish meal prices 
rose from approximately Rs. 100 per kg to 
approximately Rs. 230 per kg between May 
and June 2026 – effectively doubling in two 
months – driven by the export of 75–80% of 
domestically manufactured fish meal, a GST 
structure that favours export over local sale, 
and uncertainty around agricultural output 
due to El Niño conditions. Soya bean meal 
costs have risen by approximately 45% in the 
same period.
The Company, together with the Feed 
Manufacturers Association and CLFMA, is 
actively representing to the Government 
to regulate the outflow of fish meal and 
permit limited import of soya bean meal 
to stabilise prices. A feed price increase is 
being prepared to recover as much of the 
cost increase as market conditions allow.
FY 2026-27 will be a challenging year for 
feed margins. The feed division PBT margin 
is expected in the range of 8–10%, against 
15.50% in FY 2025-26. Feed volumes are 
targeted at approximately 5,80,000 MT.
The anchor holds. The course may require 
adjustment. But the destination remains 
clear.

From Source to Global Shelf  
	 Processed Shrimp
There is a particular kind of performance 
that speaks loudest – the kind delivered not 
in a favourable market, but through one of 
the most disruptive years in recent memory 
for Indian seafood exporters.
In FY 2025-26, Avanti Frozen Foods Private 
Limited delivered exactly that kind of 
performance.
This performance was achieved in a year 
when the US – historically the single largest 
buyer of Indian shrimp – imposed a 50% 
reciprocal tariff on Indian goods for the 
better part of the year. U.S. export volumes 
industry-wide fell by 17.9% in FY 2025-26.
The Diversification That Made the Difference
European Union volumes rose by 5%. Japan 
grew by 45%. Korea, Canada and Middle 
East demand grew steadily. The market map 
of FY 2025-26 reads very differently from 
FY 2024-25 – and AFFPL had been building 
these relationships for several years before 
the disruption arrived.
The strategic commitment to value-added 
products – cooked, breaded, marinated and 
ready-to-eat shrimp – proved its importance 
in a year where pricing discipline mattered 
as much as volume. Where commodity 
products compete on price, value-added 
products compete on relationship.
The Tariff Resolution
Following the U.S. Supreme Court's ruling 
of 20th February 2026 and the subsequent 
bilateral 
trade 
understanding 
reducing 
the effective U.S. tariff to 18%, AFFPL – as 
importer of record in the US – is pursuing 
refunds of tariffs collected, estimated at 
approximately USD 15–20 million through 
the U.S. Customs CAPE processing system.
With a strengthened product range, proven 
market relationships, and a structurally 
improved trade environment, Avanti Frozen 
Foods enters FY 2026-27 in a position of 
genuine strength.

The future of shrimp exports is not only 
about volume.
It is about value.
During FY 2025-26, Avanti increased its 
focus on value-added products, supported 
by evolving customer preferences and the 
need to improve realisations across export 
destinations.
Value-added products bring several com-
pounding advantages:
They improve customer loyalty & retention. 
They reduce pure commodity exposure. They 
support margin resilience. They allow better 
alignment with premium retail and food 
service demand. They strengthen Avanti's 
position in sophisticated global markets.
The Company's product portfolio across raw, 
cooked, breaded, marinated and ready-to-
cook formats enables it to serve a wider set 
of customer requirements – from institutional 
buyers to premium retail chains.
As global seafood consumption evolves, 
convenience, quality, traceability and product 
consistency 
are 
becoming 
increasingly 
important. Avanti's value-added strategy is 
aligned with this direction.
It marks a shift from supplying 
product to delivering solutions.
And that shift is central to the Company's 
next phase of growth.

Strength at the Source
Every successful shrimp crop begins before 
the feed is used and before the harvest is 
planned.
It begins with quality seed.
Avanti's Hatchery Division – located in 
Gudiwada village, Visakhapatnam district, 
Andhra Pradesh – plays an important role 
in the Company's integrated aquaculture 
ecosystem, supporting farmers with high-
quality post-larvae and scientific hatchery 
practices.
FY 2025-26 was a difficult year for the 
hatchery 
division. 
Challenging 
market 
conditions affected activity levels and the 
segment reported a loss. The Company is 
actively reviewing broodstock management, 
biosecurity 
protocols 
and 
production 
economics to improve performance in FY 
2026-27.
Yet strategically, the hatchery remains an 
important link in Avanti's long-term value 
chain. It strengthens the Company's ability to 
support farmers at the beginning of the crop 
cycle. It reinforces quality consciousness. 
It enables better engagement across the 
farming ecosystem.
In aquaculture, strength at the source shapes 
strength across the chain.
Advanced 
pathogen 
screening, 
genetic 
evaluation and disease surveillance underpin 
every batch of post-larvae that leaves 
the Gudiwada facility – providing farmers 
with seed matched to seasonal conditions, 
regional 
disease 
patterns 
and 
pond 
management capability.

Opening New Waters
Some growth journeys begin within the core.
Others begin by recognising how core capa-
bilities can travel into new categories.
Avanti's entry into pet care represents one 
such journey – built on more than three de-
cades of experience in nutrition, sourcing, 
quality management and food processing.
The result: Avant Furst. Avanti's premium pet 
care brand.
India's pet food market is growing rapidly 
– driven by rising pet ownership, increasing 
awareness of pet health, and the genera-
tional shift in the relationship between fami-
lies and companion animals. It is a consumer 
category of significant and expanding scale. 
For Avanti, this is not a distant adjacency. It 
is a natural extension of what the Company 
understands deeply –nutrition, quality, trust 
and consistency.
The Opportunity Ahead
Every category that Avanti has entered – 
shrimp feed in 1993, processing in 2003, 
hatchery in 2009 – began as a small invest-
ment in a large long-term opportunity. Pet 
care follows the same logic. India is at the be-
ginning of its pet care market development. 
The Company is entering while the market 
is young, building brand relationships and 
distribution depth that will compound as the 
category grows.
In charting new waters, Avanti 
is carrying forward the same 
discipline that built its core.
Avant Furst is Avanti’s next category – built 
on three decades of nutrition, sourcing and 
quality expertise.

Chairman's Message
Dear Shareholders, 
FY 2025–26 was a year marked by 
significant complexity. Shifts in U.S. trade 
policy, geopolitical tensions in West Asia, 
and rising raw material costs tested the 
resilience of our industry. Yet, as we have 
always believed at Avanti, a changing tide 
becomes a challenge only when one lacks 
the skill to navigate it. Our sails remained 
firm in turbulent weathers 
I am pleased to report that the Company 
steered 
through 
this 
demanding 
environment with clarity, discipline, and 
consistency.
On a consolidated basis, total revenue 
reached `6,276 crore, registering an 8.9% 
increase over the previous year. Profit Before 
Tax from continuing operations rose to `893 
crore from `737 crore in FY 2024–25. Profit 
After Tax stood at `657 crore, while Earnings 
Per Share improved to `44.48 from `38.81. 
The Board has recommended a dividend of 
`10 per equity share. These results affirm 
the strength and durability of our business 
model, built over three decades on deep 
farmer relationships, technical excellence, 
and prudent financial management.
Strength in the Core Feed Business
The Shrimp Feed Division continued to serve 
as the bedrock of our operations. Despite 
near-flat revenue, segment profitability 
improved meaningfully, with results rising 
to `568.25 crore from `525.30 crore on 
volumes of 5,62,060 metric tonnes. In April 
2025, we proactively reduced feed prices 
to support farmer economics — a decision 
that reflects our long-standing commitment 
to the aquaculture community.
At Avanti, feed is more than a product; it is 
a relationship built on trust. Our technical 
teams remained closely engaged with 
farmers 
through 
field 
advisory, 
pond 
management 
support, 
and 
crop-cycle 
guidance. This partnership proved to be one 
of our greatest strengths amid uncertainty.
Sharp increases in key raw material costs, 
particularly fish meal and soya bean 
meal, were managed effectively through 
disciplined procurement and operational 
efficiencies. As we enter FY 2026–27, cost 
pressures have intensified. We continue 
to engage with the Government, the Feed 
Manufacturers Association, and CLFMA to 
address structural issues and will implement 
necessary 
price 
revisions 
as 
market 
conditions permit.
Processed Shrimp: A Standout 
Performance
The Processed Shrimp business delivered 
an 
exceptional 
performance. 
Segment 
revenue grew 43.14% to `1,689.46 crore from 
`1,180.27 crore, while segment results more 
than doubled to `128.25 crore from `48.61 
crore. This was achieved despite a 50% 
reciprocal tariff on Indian goods in the U.S. 
market for part of the year. We successfully 
diversified our customer base across Japan, 
Europe, Korea, Canada, and the Middle East, 
significantly reducing market concentration 
risk. With improving trade dynamics, the 
India–EU Free Trade Agreement, and the 
India–UK CETA, we are well positioned 
to 
accelerate 
growth 
through 
market 
diversification, value-added products, and 
stronger customer partnerships.
Building New Platforms
Avanti Pet Care Private Limited made an 
encouraging debut with the launch of cat 
and dog food products under the Avant 
30 | Annual Report 2025-26 

Furst brand. Plans are underway for a 
manufacturing facility near Hyderabad, with 
commercial production expected in early 
2028. Pet food venture is self-funded and 
embody our commitment to disciplined, 
long-term value creation.
Gratitude
None of these achievements would have 
been 
possible 
without 
the 
continued 
trust of our farmers, the dedication of our 
employees, the support of our channel 
partners and customers, and the confidence 
of our shareholders. I extend my sincere 
gratitude to every member of the Avanti 
family and to my colleagues on the Board 
for their wise counsel and steadfast support.
As we enter FY 2026–27, we remain vigilant 
to near-term challenges while staying 
confident in the robustness of our core 
business, our strong financial foundation, 
and the promising new platforms we are 
nurturing.
The tides will continue to shift. At Avanti, 
we will navigate them with discipline, 
responsibility, and purpose.

MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS
Caveat
This section of the Annual Report has been prepared in accordance with the spirit of Corporate Gov-
ernance requirements prescribed by the Securities and Exchange Board of India ("SEBI"). The discus-
sion herein reflects the Management's perception of the Company's operating environment, industry 
developments, opportunities, risks, performance, and outlook as at the date of this report. Statements 
made in this section may include forward-looking views based on current assumptions and available 
information. Actual results may differ materially due to changes in economic conditions, trade poli-
cies, tariffs, input costs, foreign exchange rates, geopolitical developments, climatic conditions, disease 
outbreaks, logistics disruptions, and other external factors. The Company undertakes no obligation to 
publicly update or revise these statements, except as may be required under applicable laws.
Global Economy
The global economy in FY 2025-26 demonstrated unexpected resilience in the face of persistent trade 
tensions, heightened policy uncertainty, and intensifying geopolitical risks. The IMF projected global 
growth at 3.1% in 2026 and 3.2% in 2027 (market-exchange-rate basis), reflecting moderate expansion 
but below pre-pandemic trends. The World Bank projected global growth to ease to 2.6% in 2026 be-
fore recovering to 2.7% in 2027.
The dominant feature of the FY 2025-26 macro-economic landscape was the sweeping recalibration 
of global trade policy by the United States, which announced an across-the-board reciprocal tariff 
structure in April 2025 and subsequently raised tariffs on Indian goods to 50% from 27th August 2025 
(a 25% baseline plus an additional 25% penal duty linked to India's purchases of Russian crude oil). The 
tariff regime was challenged in U.S. courts, and on 20th February 2026 the U.S. Supreme Court ruled 
that the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) does not authorise the U.S. President 
to impose tariffs on imports. Separately, on 2nd February 2026, the U.S. and India concluded a bilateral 
trade understanding under which the reciprocal tariff on Indian goods was reduced from 50% to 18%.
Alongside the tariff disruption, escalating geopolitical tensions in West Asia resulted in continued dis-
ruption to the Red Sea–Suez Canal shipping corridor. Ocean freight rates, container availability, transit 
times, and marine insurance premiums all remained volatile through the year. For perishable cargo 
such as frozen seafood, this translated into extended lead times, elevated cold-chain costs, and more 
complex logistics planning at destination markets. However, demand for quality seafood and protein-
rich food products continued to remain structurally relevant across developed and emerging markets.
Global Economy Vs Indian Economy
Compared with several advanced economies, India continued to remain one of the more resilient and 
fastest-growing major economies globally. The World Bank and the IMF both noted India as the fastest-
growing large economy, supported by strong domestic consumption, sustained public investment, dig-
ital adoption, infrastructure development, and a stable financial system. The Ministry of Statistics and 
Programme Implementation (MoSPI) estimated India's real GDP growth at around 7.4% for FY 2025-26 
and the projected growth for FY 2026-27 is from 5.7% to 6.9%. The S&P sovereign rating upgrade in 
August 2025 — India's first in 18 years — reinforced confidence in India's macroeconomic trajectory.
India's relatively strong macroeconomic position supported sectors linked to consumption, agricul-
ture, food processing, and exports. However, the economy also remained exposed to external risks, 
including crude oil volatility, geopolitical developments, global trade barriers, currency movements, 
and weather-related uncertainty. For the seafood sector, India's long coastline, established farming 
base, processing capabilities, skilled manpower, and export infrastructure continue to provide a strong 
structural foundation, while tariff exposure in key markets and logistics disruptions underline the need 
for diversification, value addition, and operational efficiency.

Salient Features of the Indian Economy
•	
Fast-growing major economy: India continues to remain among the fastest-growing large 
economies, supported by consumption, services, infrastructure, and public investment.
•	
Strong domestic demand: Rising income levels, urbanisation, and consumption growth continue 
to support domestic market expansion.
•	
Infrastructure development: Investments in roads, ports, cold chains, logistics, and digital 
infrastructure are strengthening the competitiveness of manufacturing and export-linked sectors.
•	
Landmark trade agreements: FY 2025-26 saw the conclusion of the India-EU Free Trade Agreement 
(27th January 2026) and the India-UK CETA, which provides 100% duty-free access for most 
Indian seafood products. The India-US tariff understanding of 2nd February 2026 reduced the 
reciprocal tariff from 50% to 18%.
•	
Export diversification: India achieved record seafood exports in FY 2025-26, supported by the 
industry’s active diversification into the European Union, South East Asia, Japan and other non-
U.S. destinations.
•	
Policy support: Government schemes such as the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana and 
the Export Promotion Mission (Rs. 25,000 crore, announced 12th November 2025) continue to 
support fisheries, aquaculture infrastructure, and exports.
Global Aquaculture and Seafood Industry Overview
The global aquaculture and seafood industry passed through a year of transition. Demand conditions 
improved gradually after a period of subdued consumption, but recovery remained uneven across re-
gions. Trade policy changes, tariff uncertainty, shipping disruptions, freight volatility, and geopolitical 
tensions influenced global seafood flows.
The most significant structural development in the global shrimp market during the year was the mod-
eration of Ecuador's aggressive pricing. Ecuador, which had long maintained a cost advantage built 
on fiscal subsidies — including on electricity, tax waivers, and preferential financing – saw this advan-
tage erode following fiscal corrections. For the first time in nearly four years, farmgate prices between 
Ecuador and India converged, materially improving pricing discipline across the global shrimp market 
and supporting better realisation prospects for Indian exporters.
Demand from markets such as Europe, Japan, Korea, and other non-U.S. destinations gained increas-
ing importance. Market diversification became a critical priority for shrimp exporters globally. The year 
reinforced the importance of supply chain agility, cost discipline, quality assurance, traceability, and 
value-added product capabilities.
Aquaculture and Seafood Sector – Indian Scenario
India remains one of the leading players in global seafood exports, with frozen shrimp continuing to 
be the dominant product category. According to final data released by the Marine Products Export 
Development Authority (MPEDA), India's seafood exports touched a record Rs. 73,890.46 crore (US$ 
8.46 billion) in FY 2025-26, with shipments of 19.72 lakh metric tonnes. Frozen shrimp remained the 
leading export item, contributing Rs. 49,037.93 crore (US$ 5,624.48 million), accounting for 40.19% of 
export quantity and 66.52% of export earnings in dollar terms. Frozen shrimp exports stood at 7,92,647 
metric tonnes in FY 2025-26, registering growth of 13.16% in rupee value and 8.64% in dollar value over 
the previous year.
Despite the strong long-term opportunity, the sector faced multiple challenges during the year — in-
cluding U.S. tariff uncertainty, increased raw material costs, disruptions in West Asian shipping routes, 
higher logistics costs, freight volatility, and changing buying behaviour in global markets. However, 
India's structural advantages remained intact: a large farming base, established processing capacities, 
skilled manpower, cost competitiveness, technical know-how, and growing focus on traceability and 
sustainability.

Company Overview and Performance
FY 2025-26 was a year of changing tides for Avanti Feeds Limited. The Company operated in an envi-
ronment shaped by tariff uncertainty, evolving global demand patterns, geopolitical disruptions, higher 
raw material costs, and logistics-related challenges. Despite these headwinds, Avanti delivered a resil-
ient performance, supported by its integrated business model, strong farmer relationships, diversified 
operations, and focus on value-added growth.
On a consolidated basis, revenue from operations increased to Rs. 6,065.86 crore in FY 2025-26 from 
Rs. 5,598.69 crore in FY 2024-25, reflecting growth of 8.34%. Total revenue from continuing and dis-
continued operations stood at Rs. 6,278.89 crore compared with Rs. 5,765.80 crore in the previous year, 
a growth of 8.90%. Profit Before Tax from continuing operations (after exceptional item) increased to 
Rs. 880.27 crore from Rs. 737.26 crore, a growth of 19.40%. Net Profit from continuing and discontinued 
operations stood at Rs. 656.80 crore compared with Rs. 557.05 crore in FY 2024-25. Basic Earnings 
Per Share (continuing and discontinued operations combined) improved to Rs. 44.48 from Rs. 38.81.
The year also saw a significant improvement in the performance of the Processed Shrimp segment, 
which delivered strong revenue and profit growth supported by improved realisations, favourable for-
eign exchange movements, an improved product mix, and better operating conditions. The Shrimp 
Feed business remained broadly stable in revenue terms while improving profitability. The Board has 
recommended a dividend of Rs. 10 per equity share of face value Re. 1 each, subject to approval of 
shareholders.
Segment-wise Performance
Shrimp Feed Division
The Shrimp Feed Division continued to be the largest contributor to the Company's business. On a con-
solidated basis, segment revenue stood at Rs. 4,366.81 crore in FY 2025-26 compared with Rs. 4,397.67 
crore in FY 2024-25, a marginal decline of 0.70%, attributable to a price reduction of Rs. 4 per kg imple-
mented in April 2025 in support of farmer economics. Segment results improved to Rs. 558.54 crore 
from Rs. 527.02 crore, reflecting growth of 5.98%. Segment margin improved from 11.98% to 12.79%.
The feed business faced pressure from rising raw material costs through the year. The Company man-
aged this environment through weighted-average inventory management, operating discipline, and 
sustained farmer engagement. The feed division’s PBT margin for FY 2025-26 stood at 15.50% com-
pared with 14.34% in FY 2024-25, supported by the fuller impact of stabilised raw material prices 
through most of the year. Feed volumes increased to 5,62,060 MT in FY 2025-26 from 5,55,248 MT in 
FY 2024-25.
Avanti reinforced its position in the shrimp feed market through consistent feed quality, field-level 
technical support, farmer advisory services, disease management guidance, and strong distribution 
reach. The Company's estimated market share remains approximately 51% to 53% of the Indian shrimp 
feed market. During the Q2 monsoon period, heavy and untimely rainfall in key shrimp-producing 
regions caused premature harvest and localised disease outbreaks; the Company's technical teams 
worked closely with affected farmers on remedial measures, and cultivation activity recovered through 
the latter part of the year.

Processed Shrimp Division
The Processed Shrimp Division — operated through the Company's subsidiary, Avanti Frozen Foods 
Private Limited (AFFPL) — delivered a strong performance in FY 2025-26. On a consolidated basis, 
segment revenue increased to Rs. 1,689.46 crore from Rs. 1,180.27 crore, registering growth of 43.14%. 
Segment results increased to Rs. 128.25 crore from Rs. 48.61 crore, a growth of 163.81%. Segment mar-
gin improved from 4.12% to 7.59%.
This performance was driven by improved price realisations, favourable foreign exchange movements, 
growth in value-added products, better product mix, improved operating leverage, and the Company's 
success in passing on the reciprocal tariff cost to U.S. customers during the peak duty period. The 
performance validated the Company's strategic focus on value-added products and market diversifi-
cation. During the year, Avanti continued to expand its customer relationships across Japan, Europe, 
Canada, Korea, the Middle East, and domestic markets, while maintaining its presence in the U.S. This 
calibrated diversification helped reduce concentration risk and aligned the business with a broader 
demand base. The Company’s shrimp export volumes grew to 16,976 MT in FY 2025-26 from 14,149 MT 
in FY 2024-25, an increase of 2,827 MT. The Division’s installed processing capacity is approximately 
26,000–28,000 MT per annum, and the strategic focus for FY 2026-27 is on improving capacity utilisa-
tion and expanding value-added product offerings rather than incremental capacity addition.
Further, the shrimp processing plant at Gopalapuram, Andhra Pradesh, has been renovated with state-
of-the-art machinery and modern processing systems. These upgrades are expected to enhance oper-
ational efficiency, improve product quality, and strengthen the Company's manufacturing capabilities.
Despite ongoing geopolitical challenges, the Company continues to maintain a strong order book, driv-
en by the superior quality and diverse range of its product portfolio. Encouraged by robust demand, 
the Company is also focused on increasing capacity utilisation during FY 2026–27 to meet the growing 
demand and support its future growth plans.
Shrimp Hatchery Division
The Shrimp Hatchery segment — reported as a separate segment in FY 2025-26 — recorded revenue 
of Rs. 12.46 crore compared with Rs. 21.68 crore in FY 2024-25. The segment reported a loss of Rs. 5.52 
crore against a profit of Rs. 3.13 crore in the previous year. The performance was affected by challeng-
ing market conditions and subdued activity in the segment. The Company continues to monitor the 
business environment and will take suitable steps to improve performance through better productivity, 
brood-stock management, and cost efficiency.
Strategic Diversification Initiatives
Value-added Products
Value-added products emerged as a key strategic focus area during the year. The strong growth in Pro-
cessed Shrimp segment revenue and profitability reflects the increasing importance of moving up the 
value chain. Value-added products support better realisations, improved customer stickiness, reduced 
commodity exposure, improved margin resilience, and stronger market positioning. The Company con-
tinues to expand its value-added offerings across suitable export markets, supported by its processing 
capabilities, customer relationships, and quality systems.
Pet Care Segment
The Company's entry into the pet care segment represents a significant strategic extension of its core 
expertise in nutrition, sourcing, processing, and quality management. Through Avanti Pet Care Private 
Limited, a subsidiary established in joint venture with Bluefalo Petcare Co. Ltd., Thailand, the Company 
is entering a fast-growing domestic consumer category aligned with rising pet ownership, urbanisa-
tion, and increasing willingness to spend on pet nutrition.
The Company has initiated market development under the “Avant Furst” brand. Cat food (Ocean Fish 
and Tuna flavours) and dog food (chicken and vegetable flavour) have been introduced in the market. 
Distribution coverage has expanded to 31 distributors across 13 cities, with the Company progressively 
entering Tier-2 and Tier-3 markets. E-commerce channels including Amazon and Supertails supple-
ment the distribution network. Revenue scaled progressively through the year, with Q4 FY26 sales

reaching Rs. 151 lakhs, up from Rs. 136 lakhs in Q3 FY26, reflecting growing product acceptance. Pro-
duction volumes have ramped from approximately 53 MT to 100 MT and are targeted at approximately 
800 MT by end of FY 2026-27. Products are currently sourced from Thailand in accordance with the 
Company’s own formulations and quality specifications; the transition to in-house manufacturing is ex-

Response to Trade and Logistics Disruptions
FY 2025-26 highlighted the importance of agility in global seafood trade. The U.S. tariff escalation 
during FY 2025-26 — beginning at 26% in April 2025, escalating to 50% from 27th August 2025, and 
ultimately reduced to 18% on 2nd February 2026 following a bilateral trade understanding — materially 
affected Indian shrimp exports to the U.S. before subsequent easing restored market visibility. In ad-
dition, geopolitical tensions in West Asia affected shipping routes, increased transit times, and raised 
freight and insurance costs.
The Company responded through six key pillars:
•	
Active market diversification: The Company accelerated its expansion into Japan, Korea, the 
European Union, the Middle East, and Canada. Industry-wide non-U.S. exports grew 30% year-on-
year to US$ 1.38 billion in the first five months of FY26 from US$ 1.06 billion in the corresponding 
period.
•	
Acceleration of value-added product strategy: The Company strengthened its focus on cooked, 
breaded, and ready-to-eat shrimp — categories where margins are higher and pricing pressure is 
comparatively less acute.
•	
Supply chain and freight management: Against the backdrop of the Red Sea–Suez Canal 
disruption, the Company strengthened logistics planning, vessel routing, container management, 
and marine insurance arrangements. Moderation in freight rates in certain trade corridors during 
the year contributed to the improvement in processing-segment margins.
•	
Capital expenditure discipline: The Company exercised prudent capital allocation, placing further 
expansion of shrimp feed and processing capacity on hold during the year while continuing to 
invest in maintenance, R&D, and the new pet food and fish feed verticals.
Following the reduction of the U.S. reciprocal tariff to 18% in February 2026, and the conclusion of 
the India-EU FTA and India-UK CETA, India’s export market outlook has improved materially from the 
conditions prevailing in the middle of the year. Separately, following the U.S. Supreme Court’s ruling 
on 20th February 2026 (6–3 majority) that the IEEPA does not authorise the imposition of tariffs, U.S. 
Customs and Border Protection (CBP) discontinued the collection of IEEPA-based tariffs with effect 
from 24th February 2026 and initiated refund proceedings. To facilitate large-scale refund process-
ing, CBP launched the Consolidated Administration and Processing of Entries (CAPE) functionality 
within its Automated Commercial Environment (ACE) on 20th April 2026. Avanti Frozen Foods Pri-
vate Limited, as the importer of record in the United States, is in the process of filing entries through 
the ACE portal to claim refunds on IEEPA tariffs paid. The quantum of potential refunds is estimated 
at approximately USD 15–20 million; however, since most entries relating to frozen shrimp from India 
remain suspended pending completion of anti-dumping and countervailing duty reviews (expected to 
conclude over 12–18 months), the actual processing and crediting of refunds is expected to follow the 
lifting of those suspensions.
Financial Performance
The following discussion is based on the audited financial results for the year ended 31st March 2026.

Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities and Threats
Strengths
Avanti Feeds Limited is one of India's leading shrimp feed companies with more than three decades of 
experience in the aquaculture sector. Its strong farmer relationships, technical expertise, distribution 
reach, and long-standing collaboration with Thai Union have enabled it to build a trusted and differenti-
ated position in the industry. The Company's integrated business model — covering feed, processing, 
exports, and emerging adjacent areas such as pet care and fish feed — provides resilience and flex-
ibility. Its focus on quality, feed performance, farmer support, and value-added products strengthens 
its competitive position. An estimated market share of approximately 51% to 53% in the Indian shrimp 
feed market underscores its leadership position.
The Company also has a strong financial base. Total consolidated equity stood at Rs. 3,707.99 crore as 
at 31st March 2026. Standalone borrowings are negligible (total finance cost for FY 2025-26 was Rs. 

Corporate Overview | Statutory Reports | Financial Reports | Notice  |  77
0.64 crore), and the Company has the financial flexibility to pursue strategic diversification opportuni-
ties without external borrowing.
Weaknesses
The Company operates in an industry exposed to external variables beyond its control — climatic con-
ditions, disease outbreaks, raw material price volatility, shrimp price fluctuations, export dependency, 
tariff changes, and logistics disruptions. The feed business is sensitive to raw material costs, while the 
export business is exposed to currency movements, freight costs, and global demand cycles. The full 
extent of cost increases cannot always be immediately passed on through price increases, creating 
periods of margin compression. The Company manages these challenges through inventory discipline, 
forex hedging, and continuous engagement with the Government on supportive policy frameworks.
Opportunities
The long-term opportunity for aquaculture and seafood remains strong, supported by rising global de-
mand for protein-rich and healthy food products. India's record seafood exports in FY 2025-26 under-
score the strength of the sector and the opportunity for organised players with quality and processing 
capabilities. Key opportunities include:
•	
India-EU FTA: Expected to enter into force in early 2027, will progressively eliminate tariffs of 12% 
to 26% on Indian shrimp into the EU — the world's largest single seafood market.
•	
India-UK CETA: Grants 100% duty-free access for most seafood products to the UK market, 
eliminating tariffs of up to 21.5%.
•	
US-India tariff improvement: The reduction of the U.S. reciprocal tariff on Indian goods from 50% 
to 18% effective 2nd February 2026 has materially improved India's price competitiveness in the 
U.S. market.
•	
Ecuador's competitive correction: Convergence of India-Ecuador farmgate prices for the first 
time in nearly four years supports better global pricing discipline.
•	
Pet food and fish feed: Fast-growing consumer categories that leverage Avanti's core expertise 
in nutrition, sourcing, processing, and quality management.
•	
Export Promotion Mission: Government's Rs. 25,000 crore mission announced 12th November 
2025 provides priority support to tariff-affected sectors including marine products.
Threats
The industry continues to face risks from global trade barriers, U.S. tariff uncertainty, West Asia logis-
tics disruption, freight volatility, insurance and war-risk costs, disease outbreaks, climate risks, and raw 
material price increases. Additional regulatory risks include:
•	
Market volatility and tariff uncertainty: The U.S. Administration introduced a temporary global 
import surcharge under Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974, effective 24th February 2026 for 
up to 150 days, initially fixed at 10%, with indications of a possible increase; the final position is 
awaited.
•	
Patikari Power impairment and associate risk: The cloudburst on 1st July 2025 severely damaged 
PPPL's 16 MW hydel plant; the Company has recognised an impairment provision accordingly.
•	
Labour Codes — Regulatory Impact: On 21st November 2025, the Government of India notified 
four Labour Codes consolidating 29 existing labour laws. The Company has assessed and recorded 
the incremental financial impact of Rs. 10.90 crore (consolidated) and Rs. 8.51 crore (standalone) 
for FY 2025-26, pertaining to gratuity and leave encashment provisions.
•	
Domestic feed competition: The customs duty on imported shrimp feed has been reinstated at 
5% in the FY 2026-27 Union Budget; monitoring competitive intensity remains important.
The Company continues to address these risks through diversification, cost discipline, farmer engage-
ment, forex management, value addition, and operational controls.

Future Outlook for India's Aquaculture and Seafood Sector
The outlook for India's aquaculture and seafood sector remains positive over the medium to long term. 
India achieved record seafood exports in FY 2025-26, reflecting the sector's underlying resilience de-
spite trade and logistics challenges. Growth is expected to be supported by improving global demand, 
value-added product opportunities, market diversification, government support, traceability and sus-
tainability initiatives, and India's cost and quality competitiveness.
The combination of the India-EU FTA expected to enter into force in early 2027, the India-UK CETA 
granting 100% duty-free access, the U.S. tariff rollback, Ecuador's competitive correction, and sus-
tained domestic policy support — together represent a structurally favourable confluence that has not 
been seen by the Indian shrimp sector in recent memory.
For Avanti, the focus will remain on strengthening the shrimp feed business, expanding value-added 
products, improving processing profitability, diversifying exports, developing pet care and fish feed 
businesses, and sustaining long-term shareholder value. The Company believes that its integrated busi-
ness model, strong farmer relationships, technical expertise, and prudent financial management posi-
tion it well to navigate changing market conditions and capture future opportunities. Feed sales in FY 
2026-27 are estimated at approximately 5,80,000 MT; shrimp processing export volumes are targeted 
at approximately 19,000 MT. The Company does not foresee any significant capital expenditure in the 
next two years, with the focus remaining on improving capacity utilisation and value-added product 
expansion within existing facilities. However, FY 2026-27 is expected to be a challenging year for the 
aquaculture industry. The prices of major raw materials — fish meal and soya bean meal — have risen 
steeply since May 2026, attributable to the geopolitical situation in West Asia and the threat of El Niño 
conditions impacting agricultural output. Fish meal prices, which stood at approximately Rs. 100 per 
kg at the start of the current year, rose to approximately Rs. 240 per kg by June 2026, representing a 
near-doubling within two months. Soya bean meal prices have also increased by approximately 45% 
over the same period, compounded by a Government of India increase in the Minimum Support Price 
of soybean by approximately Rs. 380 per quintal to Rs. 5,708 per quintal. A significant contributing 
factor to the fish meal shortage is the diversion of 75–80% of domestically manufactured fish meal to 
exports, incentivised by higher export price realisation and Government export incentives, while local 
buyers face a 5% GST on domestic purchases not applicable on exports. The Company, along with the 
Feed Manufacturers Association and CLFMA, is actively representing to the Government to regulate 
fish meal availability through limiting export quantities and withdrawal of export incentives; it is also 
approaching the Government for permission to import soya bean meal on a limited basis to stabilise 
prices. The Company intends to increase feed prices to compensate for higher raw material costs to 
the extent feasible while preserving farmer economics. 
POWER
The Company sold its windmill asset during the year as part of its strategy to streamline non-core as-
sets. The discontinued wind power operation recorded Profit After Tax of Rs. 1.05 crore in FY 2025-26 
compared with Rs. 0.17 crore in FY 2024-25. The divestment has had no material impact on the ongo-
ing operations of the Company.
Srivathsa Power Projects Private Limited (SPPPL), a wholly-owned subsidiary, operates a 17.2 MW gas-
based independent power project in Andhra Pradesh. The plant remained non-operational during FY 
2025-26 due to non-availability of APM gas, following the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas di-
rective (issued in July 2022) under which APM gas from the KG basin allocated to power plants was 
diverted to CGD entities.
Patikari Power Private Limited (PPPL), in which the Company holds a 25.89% equity interest as an 
Associate, operates a 16 MW Hydel Power Project on the Beas River in Himachal Pradesh. On 1st July 
2025, the plant sustained severe damage following a cloudburst that destroyed major infrastructure 
including the approach road, dam site, and powerhouse. After assessing the facts and applying the rel-
evant accounting standards, the Company has recognised an impairment provision on its investment in 
PPPL. The consolidated exceptional item stands at Rs. 12.97 crore and the standalone exceptional item 
stands at Rs. 10.65 crore for FY 2025-26.

At Avanti Feeds Limited, sustainability remains integral to our long-term strategy 
and business resilience. We are committed to creating enduring value through 
responsible governance, environmental stewardship, social inclusion, and ethical 
business conduct, while supporting the sustainable development of the aquaculture 
ecosystem. Our Business Responsibility and Sustainability framework continues to 
guide our decisions, ensuring that growth is aligned with stakeholder expectations 
and global sustainability imperatives. 
Environmental (E)
The aquaculture sector continues to face increasing environmental challenges 
arising from climate change, extreme weather events, and volatility in the availability 
of natural resources. Variations in climatic conditions, water quality, and disease 
patterns have significant implications for shrimp farming productivity and the 
broader value chain. In response, the Company has strengthened its farmer advisory 
programmes, promoted sustainable aquaculture practices, enhanced biosecurity 
measures, and encouraged the adoption of resilient farming infrastructure. 
During the year, we further expanded our renewable energy initiatives and 
increased the share of renewable energy in our overall energy consumption. While 
overall electricity consumption increased owing to higher production volumes, 
the proportion of renewable energy usage improved, reflecting our continued 
commitment to reducing dependence on conventional energy sources. Our target 
remains to reduce grid electricity consumption by 10% by FY 2029–30 through 
energy-efficient technologies, periodic performance assessments, and sustained 
investments in clean energy solutions. 
The Company also remains committed to responsible sourcing practices, including 
the procurement of RTRS and ProTerra-certified soybean meal and participation in 
Fishery Improvement Projects (FIPs), thereby strengthening supply chain resilience 
and supporting global sustainability objectives. 
Social (S)
Our people, farming communities, and business partners constitute the foundation 
of our success. We continue to prioritize employee well-being, occupational health 
and safety, fair labour practices, and community development across all our 
operations. Recognising the inherent safety risks associated with feed manufacturing 
and hatchery operations, the Company has implemented comprehensive 
safety management systems, including dedicated safety oversight, behavioural 
interventions, engineering controls, and continuous monitoring mechanisms. 
A key focus area during the year was farmer development and capacity building. 
Through our Technical After Sales Service (TASS) teams, industry experts, and 
technical consultants, we conducted extensive training programmes covering 
best management practices, water quality management, shrimp health, disease 
prevention, biosecurity, and sustainable farming techniques. These initiatives have 
strengthened farmers’ technical capabilities, enhanced productivity, and contributed 
to the long-term sustainability of the aquaculture sector. Our commitment to 
upgrading the skills of more than 20,000 farmers remains ongoing. 
We also continue to uphold a culture founded on dignity, fairness, and inclusivity, 
supported by robust grievance redressal mechanisms, social compliance 
frameworks, and ethical labour practices that foster employee engagement and 
organizational resilience. 
Governance (G)
Strong governance practices underpin our sustainability journey. The Board and 
senior management remain actively engaged in overseeing ESG priorities, integrating 
sustainability considerations into strategic decision-making, risk management 
processes, and stakeholder engagement mechanisms. Our governance framework 
is supported by policies aligned with all nine principles of the National Guidelines 
on Responsible Business Conduct (NGRBC), reflecting our commitment to ethical, 
transparent, and accountable business conduct. 
The Company continues to strengthen supply chain governance through responsible 
sourcing requirements, supplier evaluations, and sustainability assessments 
covering environmental compliance, labour practices, and ethical standards. We 
have established a target to procure at least 50% of key raw materials through 
sustainable sources by FY 2029-30, thereby reinforcing responsible value chain 
management. 
Further, the successful completion of reasonable assurance on BRSR Core KPIs 
reflects our commitment to transparency, reliability, and stakeholder confidence in 
ESG disclosures. 
As we move forward, Avanti Feeds Limited will continue to pursue sustainable growth 
by strengthening environmental stewardship, empowering communities, fostering 
innovation, and maintaining the highest standards of corporate governance. We 
remain confident that our integrated ESG approach will enhance long-term 
resilience, create shared value for stakeholders, and contribute meaningfully to the 
sustainable development of the aquaculture industry.

Is there a mechanism available to receive and redress grievances for the following 
categories of employees and worker? If yes, give details of the mechanism in 
brief: 30
Yes/No (If Yes, then give details of the mechanism in brief)
Permanent 
Workers
Avanti Feeds Limited has instituted a strengthened and independently administered grievance 
redressal mechanism for all permanent workers during FY 2025–26. The Company has engaged a 
dedicated external agency to receive, manage, and redress complaints and grievances raised by 
employees and workers across all operational facilities. The details and contact information of the 
external agency are prominently displayed across all workplace locations including notice boards 
at manufacturing plants, hatchery facilities, and administrative offices ensuring that all workers are 
aware of the mechanism and can access it conveniently and without intermediary intervention. 
Process: Any permanent worker may directly report a complaint, concern, or grievance to the 
external agency through the designated contact channel, without the requirement to first route 
the concern through internal management. The agency is responsible for acknowledging the 
complaint, initiating appropriate enquiry or redressal action, and ensuring that the matter is 
addressed in a fair, confidential, and time-bound manner. 
Reporting to Senior Management: At the close of each calendar month, the external agency 
submits a consolidated grievance report to Senior Management, including the Chairman and 
Managing Director (CMD). This report covers all complaints received during the month, the nature 
of grievances, actions taken, and resolution status. In months where no complaints have been 
received, a Nil Complaint Report is formally submitted to Senior Management, ensuring complete 
transparency and uninterrupted oversight at the highest level of the organisation. This mechanism 
ensures independence, confidentiality, and senior-level accountability in the grievance redressal

10.	 Health and safety management system:
S.no
a)
Whether an occupational health and safety management system has been implemented by the 
entity? (Yes/ No). If yes, the coverage such system? 34
Avanti has implemented a comprehensive Occupational Health and Safety Management System 
(OHSMS) covering all its feed manufacturing plants and hatchery facility. Ensuring the health, safety, 
and well-being of every employee and worker across all operational locations remains a cornerstone 
of the Company's business conduct. The OHSMS is designed to create a safe, hygienic, and regulatory-
compliant work environment through a structured combination of safety protocols, dedicated safety 
oversight, health programmes, training initiatives, and independent audit mechanisms.
1. Dedicated In-House Safety Officer
The Company has appointed a dedicated in-house Safety Officer responsible for the day-to-day 
oversight and administration of occupational health and safety across all feed manufacturing plants and 
the hatchery facility. The Safety Officer conducts regular safety training sessions for workers, monitors 
plant operations and worker practices on the shop floor, and identifies unsafe acts, unsafe conditions, 
and machinery-related hazards requiring corrective intervention. Safety observations identified during 
shop floor monitoring are formally presented by the Safety Officer at weekly meetings with Department 
Heads (HODs), following which corrective actions are assigned, tracked, and implemented in a time-
bound manner. This governance structure ensures that safety concerns receive immediate management 
attention and are resolved systematically rather than reactively.
2. Workplace Safety Protocols
The Company adheres to stringent workplace safety regulations across all facilities, maintaining a hazard-
free work environment for all categories of workers. Employees working in feed manufacturing areas 
including high-temperature pelleting, steam conditioning, boiler operations, and raw material handling 
are provided with appropriate high-quality Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) including heat-resistant 
gloves, safety footwear, ear protection, dust masks, and other role-specific protective equipment. 
Regular safety inspections and internal audits are carried out across all facilities to proactively identify 
and mitigate risks before they result in incidents or injuries.
3. OHS Audit
An independent Occupational Health and Safety audit was conducted during FY 2025–26, covering the 
Company's feed manufacturing and hatchery operations. The audit assessed compliance with applicable 
statutory safety requirements, evaluated the effectiveness of implemented safety protocols and controls, 
and identified areas for improvement. Findings from the OHS audit are reviewed by senior management 
and incorporated into the Company's corrective action programme, ensuring continuous improvement 
in safety performance across all facilities.
4. Health and Wellness Initiatives
The Company organizes health awareness drives, periodic medical check-ups, and interactive sessions 
with healthcare professionals to promote the holistic well-being of employees across all locations. First 
aid facilities and comprehensive healthcare services are available at all operational facilities to address 
occupational and non-occupational health needs of the workforce.
5. Training and Emergency Preparedness
All employees and workers undergo regular safety training sessions covering essential topics including 
fire safety, safe handling of hazardous materials, boiler safety, and emergency response procedures. 
Frequent mock drills and emergency evacuation exercises are conducted across all facilities to ensure 
that workers are adequately prepared to respond efficiently to potential workplace incidents, minimizing 
risk to life and enabling effective containment of hazards.

b)
What are the processes used to identify work-related hazards and assess risks on a routine and 
non-routine basis by the entity?35
Avanti employs a systematic and multi-layered approach to hazard identification and risk assessment, 
covering both routine operational activities and non-routine situations such as maintenance, equipment 
commissioning, and emergency scenarios. The key processes are as follows:
1. In-House Safety Officer - Continuous Shop Floor Monitoring
The dedicated in-house Safety Officer conducts continuous monitoring of plant operations and worker 
behavior on the shop floor, enabling real-time identification of unsafe acts, unsafe conditions, and 
equipment-related hazards on a day-to-day basis. Hazards identified during monitoring are documented 
and presented at weekly HOD meetings, where corrective actions including engineering modifications 
to machinery where required are assigned and tracked to closure. This ensures that routine hazard 
identification is embedded in the Company's daily operational rhythm rather than confined to periodic 
assessments alone.
2. Weekly Safety Review Meetings with Department HODs
Safety observations collated by the Safety Officer are formally reviewed at weekly meetings with 
Department Heads across all functions. This structured review process ensures that identified hazards 
whether arising from routine operations or non-routine activities receive prompt cross-functional 
management attention and that corrective actions are implemented without delay.
3. Quarterly Risk Assessments
The Company conducts comprehensive risk assessments on a quarterly basis, covering operational, 
environmental, and safety risks associated with feed manufacturing and hatchery activities. These 
assessments proactively evaluate potential hazards across all process areas and result in the 
implementation of updated safety measures and control protocols to minimize or eliminate identified 
risks. Quarterly assessments also incorporate a review of non-routine activities scheduled for the 
upcoming period, ensuring that hazards associated with planned maintenance, equipment changes, or 
process modifications are assessed in advance.
4. Safety Drills and Protocol Testing
Regular safety drills are organized to evaluate the practical effectiveness of safety protocols under 
simulated emergency conditions. Drill outcomes are analyzed to identify gaps in hazard response 
preparedness, with findings incorporated into updated safety procedures and training programmes.
5. Employee and Field Staff Feedback
The Company maintains open communication channels with employees and field staff to gather ground-
level insights on risks encountered or anticipated during the course of operations. Feedback from workers 
particularly those directly engaged in production and hatchery processes is systematically analyzed to 
identify emerging or previously unidentified hazards, enabling proactive risk mitigation before incidents 
occur.
6. OHS Audit
An independent OHS audit was conducted during FY 2025–26, providing an external, objective 
assessment of hazard identification and risk management processes across the Company's facilities. 
Audit findings supplement internal risk assessment processes and ensure that the Company's hazard 
identification framework is benchmarked against applicable regulatory requirements and industry best 
practices.

c)
Whether you have processes for workers to report the work-related hazards and to remove 
themselves from such risks. (Yes/ No)
Yes. Avanti has established a dedicated process enabling all workers to report work-related hazards and, 
where necessary, to remove themselves from situations of imminent risk to their safety and health. The 
key elements of this process are as follows:
1. Direct Reporting to the In-House Safety Officer
Workers may directly report unsafe acts, unsafe conditions, near-miss situations, or any work-related 
hazard to the dedicated in-house Safety Officer, who is accessible across all plant and hatchery locations. 
The Safety Officer is empowered to immediately assess the reported concern, initiate corrective action 
including engineering modifications to machinery or process controls where required and escalate to 
Department HODs at the weekly safety review meeting for systemic resolution.
2. Quarterly Safety Representative Meetings
At each facility, designated safety representatives from the workforce convene on a quarterly basis with 
management to formally raise safety concerns, provide suggestions on hazard prevention, and receive 
management feedback on actions taken in response to previously reported issues. This forum ensures 
that worker voices are systematically incorporated into the Company's safety governance process.
3. Worker Feedback and Open Communication
The Company actively encourages all workers, unsafe acts, and unsafe conditions through open 
communication channels with supervisors, the Safety Officer, and HR. Workers are assured that safety 
reporting is treated as a positive and valued contribution to workplace safety, free from any risk of 
adverse consequence.
4. Right to Remove from Risk
Workers who identify an imminent and serious risk to their safety in the course of their work are 
empowered to remove themselves from the hazardous situation and report the concern immediately 
to their supervisor or the Safety Officer, pending assessment and rectification of the risk. This right is 
communicated to all workers as part of safety induction and training programmes.

Comprehensive first aid facilities and on-site healthcare services are available at all operational locations 
of the Company, ensuring that employees and workers have immediate access to medical assistance for 
both occupational and non-occupational health needs during working hours.
2. Periodic Medical Check-Ups and Health Awareness Programmes
The Company organizes periodic medical check-ups for employees, complemented by health awareness 
drives and interactive sessions with healthcare professionals covering topics such as nutrition, preventive 
healthcare, and general wellness supporting employees in managing their health proactively.
3. Continuous Safety and Health Culture
The Company fosters a culture of accountability and care across all facilities, conducting ongoing training

prevailing industry standards and applicable regulatory requirements.

Describe the measures taken by the entity to ensure a safe and healthy workplace.
Avanti recognises that a safe, healthy, and supportive workplace is fundamental to the well-being of its workforce 
and the long-term operational excellence of its business. The Company has implemented a comprehensive suite 
of health, safety, and environmental measures across all its feed manufacturing plants and hatchery facility. 
The measures in place during FY 2025–26 are as follows:
1. Dedicated Safety Leadership and Structured Management Review
The Company has appointed a dedicated in-house Safety Officer responsible for overseeing occupational health 
and safety across all operational facilities. The Safety Officer conducts regular shop floor monitoring to identify 
unsafe acts, unsafe conditions, and equipment-related hazards. Observations are formally presented at weekly 
meetings with Department Heads, where corrective actions are assigned, tracked, and resolved in a time-bound 
manner ensuring safety concerns receive immediate management attention at every level.
2. Independent Occupational Health and Safety Audit
An independent OHS audit was conducted during FY 2025–26, providing an objective third-party evaluation 
of the Company’s safety management systems and statutory compliance across its facilities. Audit findings are 
reviewed by senior management and incorporated into a structured corrective action programme. This ensures 
continuous improvement in safety performance and provides independent verification of the Company’s safety 
commitments to all stakeholders.
3. Continuous Safety Training and Capability Building
All employees and workers including new joiners, contract workers, and seasonal staff undergo mandatory safety 
induction training before commencing work at any Company facility. Ongoing refresher training conducted 
by the in-house Safety Officer covers safe machine operation, chemical handling, fire safety, and emergency 
response. Training completion is documented and monitored to ensure consistent coverage across all worker 
categories and locations.
4. Robust Incident Reporting and Investigation Process
The Company has established clear incident reporting and investigation procedures enabling all workers to 
report safety concerns and near-miss situations promptly and without apprehension. Every reported concern 
is investigated to identify root causes, implement immediate corrective measures, and develop preventive 
actions to eliminate recurrence. Investigation outcomes are reviewed by the Safety Officer and Department 
Heads, fostering a culture where safety reporting is actively encouraged and every incident drives a tangible 
improvement in workplace safety.
It establishes a clear reporting and investigation procedures to address incidents or concerns swiftly, ensuring 
quick action and continuous improvement.

Independent External Grievance Redressal Agency – Primary Complaints Channel
The Company has engaged a dedicated external agency as the primary channel for receiving and redressing 
all employee and worker complaints, including those relating to human rights concerns such as forced labour, 
discrimination, harassment, wage violations, and unsafe working conditions. Contact details of the external

Prevention of discrimination and harassment cases
Mechanisms to prevent adverse consequences to the complainant in discrimination and harassment cases 50
Avanti is firmly committed to maintaining a workplace free from all forms of discrimination, harassment, and 
intimidation. The Company has established a robust framework of preventive and remedial mechanisms to 
protect complainants from adverse consequences and ensure that every individual feels safe, respected, and 
empowered to raise concerns without fear of retaliation. 
The mechanisms in place during FY 2025–26 are as follows:
1. Independent External Agency — Primary Reporting and Protection Channel
The Company has engaged an independent external agency as the primary channel for receiving complaints 
related to discrimination, harassment, and related human rights concerns from all employees and workers. 
Contact details of the external agency are prominently displayed on notice boards across all feed manufacturing 
plants and the hatchery facility, ensuring direct and unimpeded access for every worker irrespective of their 
employment category. Since complaints are received and managed by an agency independent of the Company’s 
internal management structure, complainants are structurally protected from any risk of managerial influence, 
bias, or retaliation in the handling of their concerns. A consolidated report of all complaints received 
2. Zero-Tolerance Policy Against Discrimination and Harassment
The Company maintains an unequivocal zero-tolerance stance toward all forms of discrimination and harassment 
in the workplace including discrimination on the basis of gender, caste, religion, disability, or any other protected 
characteristic and toward sexual harassment in particular. This policy is communicated to all employees and 
workers at the time of induction and reinforced through periodic awareness programmes. Any substantiated 
instance of discrimination or harassment is treated as a serious disciplinary matter, with appropriate action taken 
against the perpetrator regardless of their seniority or role within the organization.
3. Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) — POSH Compliance
In compliance with the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 
2013, the Company has constituted Internal Complaints Committees (ICC) across its operational locations. The 
ICC is empowered to receive, investigate, and recommend resolution of complaints of sexual harassment in a fair, 
confidential, and time-bound manner. The Committee includes an external independent member as mandated 
under the POSH Act, further reinforcing the impartiality and credibility of the investigation process. All ICC 
proceedings are conducted with strict confidentiality, protecting the identity and dignity of the complainant 
throughout.
4. Awareness and Training Programmes
Regular training and awareness sessions are conducted for all employees and workers covering the recognition, 
prevention, and reporting of discrimination and harassment with particular emphasis on sexual harassment 
awareness under the POSH Act. Training is conducted by the HR function and covers available reporting 
mechanisms, the role and process of the ICC, complainant rights, and the Company’s zero-tolerance commitment. 
Training completion is documented and monitored to ensure comprehensive coverage across all worker 
categories and locations

Mechanism for Zero Liquid Discharge: 54
Has the entity implemented a mechanism for Zero Liquid Discharge? If yes, provide details of its 
coverage and implementation
Yes, Avanti Feeds has implemented a Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) system to ensure responsible water 
management and minimize environmental impact.
1. Coverage & Scope:
The ZLD system is in place across all major processing plants to treat and recycle wastewater generated during 
shrimp processing.
It applies to effluent from cleaning, washing, and processing activities, ensuring that no untreated liquid waste is 
discharged into the environment.
2. Implementation & Process:
Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP): Wastewater is treated through two ETP units, undergoing primary, secondary, 
and tertiary treatment to effectively remove contaminants.
3. Water Reuse: 
Treated water recovered from the treatment process is reused for green belt development and plantation 
activities within the Company's premises, thereby reducing freshwater consumption.
4. Solid Waste Management: 
Sludge generated from the treatment process is utilized as manure for green belt and plantation activities, 
promoting resource recovery and supporting sustainable waste management practices.
This ZLD mechanism enhances water efficiency, reduces environmental footprint, and ensures regulatory 
compliance, reinforcing Avanti Feeds commitment to sustainable and responsible operations.

Project related to reducing Green House Gas emission: 56
Does the entity have any project related to reducing Green House Gas emission? If yes, then provide details.
Yes. Avanti Feeds Limited has undertaken several projects directed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions across 
its operations. The key initiatives implemented by the Company are as follows:
Renewable Energy — Solar Energy Expansion
Rooftop solar panels have been installed across facilities, and a dedicated large-scale solar farm has been 
established to increase the share of renewable energy in the Company's total energy mix. These initiatives reduce 
Scope 2 emissions by displacing grid electricity with zero-emission solar generation.
Energy Efficiency — Equipment Upgrades and LED Lighting
The Company has upgraded to energy-efficient equipment and replaced conventional lighting with LED systems 
across all facilities. These measures reduce total electricity consumption and associated Scope 2 GHG emissions.
Water Management — Effluent Treatment and Reuse
The Company has implemented effluent treatment and water reuse systems working toward Zero Liquid 
Discharge objectives. This reduces the energy intensity of water management processes, indirectly contributing 
to overall GHG emission reduction.
Transition from Furnace Oil to Biomass Briquettes — Feed Manufacturing Plants
The Company is progressively replacing furnace oil with biomass briquettes derived from agricultural waste as the 
primary fuel for boiler and furnace operations at its feed manufacturing plants. This ongoing transition directly reduces 
Scope 1 greenhouse gas emissions by substituting a fossil fuel with a lower net-carbon agricultural by-product.
Open Access Electricity Procurement
The Company has commenced procurement of electricity through open access arrangements, diversifying 
its electricity sourcing away from conventional grid supply. This initiative supports the Company's broader 
strategy of reducing dependence on grid electricity and optimising its energy cost and supply security across 
manufacturing operations.

and contact numbers through which consumers, aqua farmers, dealers, and other stakeholders may submit 
complaints, queries, or feedback. These contact details are made available on the Company's official website

categories of consumer concerns.

The Company maintains open and proactive communication with its stakeholders including aqua farmers, dealers, 
distributors, and institutional buyers to identify and address concerns before they escalate into formal complaints. 
This engagement-first approach reflects the Company's commitment to transparency, responsiveness, and the 
maintenance of strong, trust-based relationships with its consumer base.
4. Feedback Integration for Continuous Improvement
Consumer and stakeholder feedback received through all channels is systematically reviewed and incorporated 
into the Company's product development, quality improvement, and customer service enhancement processes.

decisions, reinforcing the Company's commitment to delivering consistent quality and value across all its
